metadata.title: Developing a shared cluster construct of instructional leadership in TALIS

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2013 secondary microdata for lower-secondary mainstream schools in Denmark, Finland, Sweden, and Norway, with teachers clustered within schools. To account for unequal selection probabilities, the authors state that sampling weights were used in all analyses, applying the final school weight at the cluster (school) level and a derived pure teacher weight at the teacher level (teacher weight divided by school weight). Data were prepared using IDB Analyzer and analyzed in Mplus with multilevel modeling (MCFA/MSEM) to properly handle within-school and between-school variance. The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and it does not describe any additional preprocessing beyond excluding a low-clustering job-satisfaction item (TQ14) and omitting cases with missing data on all variables by default in Mplus WLSMV.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This paper does not analyze cognitive achievement scores with plausible values; instead, it models latent constructs from TALIS questionnaire items using multilevel confirmatory factor analysis and multilevel structural equation modeling. Because the dependent variables are latent-factor indicators (and not PV-based achievement), PV handling is not applicable. For missing data, the authors only state that Mplus WLSMV by default does not include cases with missing data on all variables, but they do not provide a complete missing-data strategy (e.g., item-level missingness rules, imputation vs. listwise behavior for partially missing cases). This is therefore a reporting gap for missing-data handling details.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary analysis of TALIS 2013 for lower-secondary (ISCED 2 level 2) teachers and leaders in mainstream schools, restricted to the Nordic countries Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and Finland (Iceland excluded due to non-authorization for international release). The analytic sample comprises 10,688 teachers clustered in 676 schools. The authors omit the teacher job-satisfaction item TQ14 from further analyses because it shows low clustering/reliability at the school level in Finland and Sweden (ICC1 low and ICC2 low). For modeling with Mplus WLSMV, the authors note that by default Mplus does not include cases with missing data on all variables; otherwise, they do not specify additional exclusion rules.

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2013 (lower-secondary) Nordic countries: Denmark, Finland, Sweden, Norway
main_findings.target_variable: Teacher job satisfaction with current work environment (school level)
main_findings.performance_metrics: MSEM regression (school level): SRMRb = 0.027–0.044 across countries; explained variance R2 < 0.02 in all countries and not statistically different from zero; standardized β estimates near zero (Denmark β = −0.04 (0.12), Finland β = −0.03 (0.11), Sweden β = −0.10 (0.09), Norway β = −0.00 (0.11)).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2013 (lower-secondary) data from Denmark, Finland, Sweden, and Norway, the study leveraged principal instructional leadership to predict teacher job satisfaction with current work environment at the school level, finding that the model fit was acceptable but instructional leadership explained less than 2% of the between-school variance and was not statistically different from zero. This indicates that the existing TALIS instructional leadership measure (based on principals’ three-item scale) may suffer from construct underrepresentation and may not capture the leadership aspects most relevant to teachers’ satisfaction, limiting its usefulness for leadership–wellbeing policy discussions.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses TALIS 2013 (lower-secondary) secondary data from Denmark, Finland, Sweden, and Norway (10,688 teachers clustered in 676 schools) to develop and validate a shared-cluster measurement approach for instructional leadership. The authors first test the existing TALIS instructional leadership scale based on principals’ three-item measure (PQ2–PQ4) and find acceptable model fit (SRMRb = 0.027–0.044) but essentially no between-school explanatory power (R2 < 0.02, not statistically different from zero). They then construct two teacher-based shared cluster dimensions—managing the instructional program and developing the school learning climate—using multilevel CFA/SEM with WLSMV and sampling weights (school weight at cluster level; pure teacher weight at teacher level). The strongest and most stable associations with teacher job satisfaction with current work environment are for developing the school learning climate (β = 0.505–0.609; R2 ≈ 0.255–0.370). Limitations include construct underrepresentation in the principal measure, strong collinearity between the two teacher-based dimensions, and incomplete reporting of missing-data handling beyond Mplus default behavior.
